title: Private Deployments: VPC & On-prem Reference Guides and Day-2 Ops Library
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document collects the canonical deployment guides, reference architectures, on-prem packaging notes, and day-2 operational procedures we use when delivering Redwood Private (VPC and on-prem) to customers. It is intended for solutions engineers, platform SREs, and customer site reliability teams who perform installs and operate Redwood in air-gapped, VPC, or hybrid environments.

Scope
- Supported deployment modes: VPC (cloud-hosted customer VPC peering or PrivateLink), customer-managed IaaS (AWS/Azure/GCP), and fully on-prem rack installs.
- Life cycle coverage: initial deployment, packaging & artifact validation, day-2 operations (monitoring, backups, scaling), and upgrade & rollback procedures.
- Not in scope: detailed application integration (use API docs in eng-developer-experience) and billing/contractual steps.

Key Contacts and Ownership
- Product owner: Priya Kaur (product)
- Private deployments engineering lead: Miguel Santos (eng)
- SRE escalation: Eve Nakamura (eng-sre)
- Solutions engineering / install lead: Rahul Iyer (customer-success)

Reference architectures (summary)
1) VPC (Cloud-hosted) — Typical topology
- Customer VPC with dedicated subnet for Redwood control plane endpoints and compute (in Dedicated mode customer-managed or in Private mode customer-hosted).
- Peering/PrivateLink to customer app VPCs for low-latency traffic.
- Optional NAT for outbound updates and telemetry (subject to compliance requirements).

Minimal network requirements (table)
| Component | Port(s) | Direction | Rationale |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Control plane API | 443 | inbound (from admin CIDR) | API / control traffic |
| Runtime nodes | 50051, 8000-8100 | inbound (from customer app VPC) | gRPC / HTTP endpoints for inference |
| KV / cache replication | 6379 (or TLS-equivalent) | bidirectional | Redis/kv cluster replication |
| Docker registry / package repo | 443 | outbound | Fetch images/updates |

2) On-prem (air-gapped) — Typical topology
- Customer datacenter with dedicated cluster(s) for Redwood runtime and control services.
- Local package repository (Nexus/Artifactory) hosting validated images and artifacts.
- Optional DMZ edge node for controlled telemetry egress via proxy or approved jump host.

Packaging and distribution model
- Artifacts provided as signed OCI images and tarball release bundles. Each release has:
  - release.yaml (version, image tags, SHA256 sums)
  - packaging checksum file: packaging.SIG
  - optional airgap bundle: redwood-airgap-<version>.tar.gz
- On-prem installs: recommended to mirror OCI registry into local registry. We provide a registry-sync script and sample manifests.

Example registry-sync command (AWS ECR as mirror target)
```
# mirror images to customer ECR
./scripts/registry-sync.sh --release 2026.04.1 --target ecr://123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/redwood
```

Validation checks (pre-install)
1. Verify checksums and signatures for all artifacts.
2. Confirm network ACLs and firewall rules align with the Minimal network requirements table.
3. Ensure KMS / HSM integration details are available for secrets encryption if required.

Day-2 operations (runbook snippets)
- Monitoring and alerting
  - Metrics: request qps, p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, cache hit ratio.
  - Alerts: latency_p99 > 1.5x SLO for 10m, GPU throttling events > 3 sustained minutes, storage_error_rate > 0.5%.
  - Dashboards: per-customer model route, per-node hardware metrics, and cluster-level capacity heatmap.

- Backups and recovery
  - Control-plane DB (Postgres) snapshot: daily logical backup + incremental WAL shipping. Retention: 14 days.
  - KV cache: warm rehydrate from persistent snapshot on node replacement (recommended snapshot frequency: hourly for high-throughput clusters).
  - Restore verification: run integration smoke tests post-restore (see smoke-tests.yaml).

Capacity and scaling
- Horizontal scaling policy: add runtime nodes when average GPU util > 72% for 5m and queue depth > 1000.
- Batching/throughput tuning: increase max_batch_size and max_latency_ms per model route; validate with perf harness (eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite).

Upgrade procedure (planned maintenance) — summary steps
1. Pre-upgrade (3 days before):
  - Communicate maintenance window to customer and internal stakeholders.
  - Run full suite of compatibility checks: release.yaml validation, model artifact compatibility matrix.
  - Create a backup snapshot of control-plane DB and store off-cluster.

2. Upgrade (canary first):
  - Deploy control-plane components with canary label to 1 node (5% traffic).
  - Monitor for 30-60 minutes for errors, latency regressions, and model inference correctness (run smoke/eval prompt set).
  - If canary passes, progressively roll to 25%, 50%, then 100% using the automated rollout pipeline (console rollout /ci/cd pipeline).

3. Post-upgrade validation (30-120 minutes after 100%):
  - Run validation suite (API health, model output checks, end-to-end latency).
  - Verify telemetry and logs are intact and retention policy enforced.

Rollback procedure (if severe regression)
- Criteria to rollback: correctness failures on evaluation prompts, latency_p99 > 2x SLO for > 30m, or repeated node-level crashes >= 3 in 15m.
- Steps:
  1) Set new release rollout to paused and switch traffic to previous release using traffic manager.
  2) Re-deploy previous control-plane manifest (use saved release.yaml and OCI image SHA).
  3) Restore DB from pre-upgrade snapshot only if schema migration failed; otherwise use backward-compatible steps.
  4) Run smoke tests and confirm system stability before marking the incident resolved.

Emergency rollback (hotfix)
- If rollback is impossible due to migrations, follow hotfix patch process (create 1.x hotfix branch, build and sign artifacts, and perform canary). Coordinate with security for rapid signing.

Upgrade checklist (short)
- [ ] Release artifacts validated (signed & checksums)
- [ ] Backups completed and stored off-cluster
- [ ] Canary plan and rollback plan documented
- [ ] Stakeholders notified
- [ ] Smoke tests & eval prompt sets ready

Customer requirements library (matrix)
| Customer requirement | Minimum Redwood requirement | Notes / Variations |
|---|---|---|
| Private network only (no egress) | Airgap bundle + local registry | Provide registry-sync helper and offline docs |
| KMS integration | KMS + key wrapping via HSM | Provide key rotation procedures and key policy examples |
| Regulatory logging retention | 365 days | Archive to customer-managed S3/GCS with immutability flags |
| High-availability (N+2) | 3+ runtime nodes per failure domain | Recommend cross-AZ deployments and redundant control-plane nodes |
| On-prem GPU servers | CUDA >= 12, NCCL compatible | Provide validated GPU driver matrix and kernel versions |

Packaging: on-prem artifact layout
- /opt/redwood/releases/<version>/release.yaml
- /opt/redwood/releases/<version>/images/  (mirrored OCI blobs)
- /opt/redwood/releases/<version>/manifests/  (k8s/helm or systemd units for non-k8s installs)
- /opt/redwood/releases/<version>/checksums/packaging.SIG

Sample release.yaml (excerpt)
```
version: "2026.04.1"
components:
  - name: control-plane
    image: registry.redwood.com/control-plane:2026.04.1@sha256:abcdef...
  - name: runtime
    image: registry.redwood.com/runtime:2026.04.1@sha256:123456...
checksums:
  - file: images.tar.gz
    sha256: 012345abcdef...
```

Operational runbooks and playbooks (links)
- See: private-deployments-vpc-onprem-deployment-runbook-2026-03-01 (detailed incident steps)
- See: private-deployments-vpc-onprem-deployment-and-day2-ops-guidance-2026-11-30 (operational best practices)

Common troubleshooting scenarios (examples)
1) High inference latency after upgrade
  - Verify new kernels / driver incompatible issues (check dmesg and driver versions).
  - Check batching config changes: revert to previous batching profile if necessary.
2) Control-plane API returning 500s intermittently
  - Check DB connections and connection pool exhaustion. Increase max_connections temporarily and scale control plane.

Appendix: SLOs and thresholds (recommended)
- Inference availability: 99.95% monthly for dedicated runtime endpoints.
- Latency: p95 <= 350ms, p99 <= 900ms for standard generation models (adjust per-model).
- Error budget policy: incidents that consume > 25% of monthly error budget require a postmortem and prioritized remediation.

Change log
